title: Safety, durability and quality
scope: Source-repository assessment. Host activation and live service status were not independently inspected. Recommendations are not deployed agents or configuration changes.
summary: The team has reusable prompts and durable shared state. Its supervisor is implemented and tested with scripted workers; the repository records no paid pilot or activated host service. Safety coverage differs by harness, and no model or harness combination can guarantee perfect results.

controls.name: Human authority
controls.description: Approvals and waivers require an owner token and a signed, hash-chained decision ledger. Editing task state does not create approval.
controls.limitation: A worker with access to the owner's token can impersonate authority. File permissions and OS isolation are still required.

controls.name: Evidence before completion
controls.description: Stage exits require their artifacts, acceptance traceability and verification. Build tasks declare executable checks; completion refuses failing checks.
controls.limitation: The CLI checks evidence structure and execution. People and reviewers must judge whether the chosen checks and artifact content are sufficient.

controls.name: Independent verification
controls.description: A builder cannot verify its own recorded task. Verification names the commit being released.
controls.limitation: Role identity is self-declared. A commit hash alone does not detect uncommitted edits; the supervisor adds a clean-tree check.

controls.name: Risk and hard human gates
controls.description: Production deployment, public publishing or messaging, spending, real credentials or payments, destructive actions, broad system changes and legal commitments remain human-controlled.
controls.layer: CLI, supported harness hooks and instructions
controls.limitation: Risk depends on truthful task declarations. Direct actions outside the CLI can escape checks when the harness has no applicable hook.

controls.name: Tool and file protections
controls.description: Supported harnesses receive hooks, permission settings or tool allowlists that protect owner material and runtime records.
controls.limitation: Coverage is not identical across harnesses. Pi and generic rely on instructions for these protections; hooks are not an OS sandbox.

controls.name: Budget and retry bounds
controls.description: Runs have ceilings, attempts reserve budget before launch, transcript usage is reconciled, and repeated failures stop retries.
controls.limitation: Usage is based on harness estimates. A running attempt can spend before its final transcript is metered; provider-side limits add another boundary.

controls.name: Recoverable execution
controls.description: The supervisor persists jobs and attempts, allows one writer per checkout, reconciles process ownership and retains uncertain cost reservations.
controls.limitation: Unclear ownership or missing records cause a hold for the owner rather than an unsafe automatic restart. This is not a permanently running model.

controls.name: Bounded unattended release
controls.description: Low-risk runs can finish the release stage without a click only with passing checks, current verification, a release packet, rehearsed rollback and no pending budget question.
controls.limitation: Every task must remain R0 or R1. This does not authorize production deployment or other external actions, and declared checks can still be incomplete.

controls.name: Controlled learning
controls.description: Lessons become candidates, are evaluated and proposed, and need human promotion before becoming proven playbook checks.
controls.layer: CLI for promotion; instructions and review for learning quality
controls.limitation: Ordinary knowledge files can be edited. The system does not prove every lesson is true or silently improve itself without evaluation.

controls.name: Regression evaluation
controls.description: Deterministic scenarios test workflow rules. The behavioral-change protocol requires pre-registered metrics, repeated baseline/candidate live runs and no score regression.
controls.layer: Automated workflow tests; opt-in live evaluation and human approval
controls.limitation: Workflow tests do not measure model intelligence. The live comparison protocol is not evidence that every model and harness has been qualified.

blockers.name: Isolation probe needs positive controls
blockers.status: Known pre-pilot correction remains in source
blockers.description: A path that does not exist inside a worker boundary can currently be mistaken for securely denied access. The probe must also prove that the worker can read the intended view and write its own home.
blockers.codeEvidence: The probe catches any OSError and prints AGENTIC-ISOLATION-DENIED or AGENTIC-VIEW-READONLY; its verified expression checks these output markers without a successful-read control.

blockers.name: Credential inheritance needs tighter filtering
blockers.status: Known pre-pilot correction remains in source
blockers.description: Anthropic and Claude credential variables are not filtered by default. The plan requires filtering them and explicitly passing only a dedicated worker credential.
blockers.codeEvidence: SENSITIVE_ENV includes OPENAI_.* and other provider prefixes, but has no ANTHROPIC_.* or CLAUDE_.* branch.

blockers.name: Host and worker paths need a verified mapping
blockers.status: Known pre-pilot setup and documentation correction
blockers.description: The worker boundary must expose the checkout, view and worker home at the paths passed by the supervisor. The pilot plan selects a POSIX host with matching absolute paths; a Windows-to-WSL prefix is not proof of that mapping.
blockers.codeEvidence: worker_argv builds values with str(self.project) and str(run_dir); verify_isolation passes str(sentinel) and str(view_dir) to the prefixed process.

blockers.name: Real-worker pilot pending
blockers.description: The repository records no paid worker pilot. Offline tests use scripted workers and cannot establish real model behavior, real boundary effectiveness or actual usage quality.

blockers.name: Persistent host activation pending
blockers.description: The repository records no registered host task. Generating a scheduler example does not activate it. Activation is a separate step after the pilot and owner decision.

durability.plainMeaning: Durable work survives a model session ending: a new worker can recover the task, evidence, decisions and progress from persistent state.
durability.promptPersistence: All 50 canonical roles have reusable source prompts. A saved prompt is not an active background agent.
durability.sharedState: The runtime persists tasks, stages, events, evidence, handoffs and knowledge. A replacement session resumes from this shared record.
durability.executionRecovery: One deterministic supervisor manages persistent jobs and bounded worker attempts per checkout. Its implementation is offline-verified; live activation is not evidenced here.
durability.rosterLabel: Reusable prompt; shared durable state; no independently activated service evidenced

supervisorAdapters.name: claude
supervisorAdapters.status: Built-in paid-worker adapter; requires a verified boundary and configured budgets; pilot pending

supervisorAdapters.name: command
supervisorAdapters.status: Owner-supplied argv; used for scripted tests; unisolated and cost reported by its own output

durability.portabilityLimit: 13 harness installation targets do not mean 13 equivalent supervisor adapters, security boundaries or model performance levels.

recommendedCore.status: Proposed operating model; not activated by this guide
recommendedCore.countMeaning: Six persistent control responsibilities, backed by one deterministic supervisor. They can run as temporary sessions with persistent identities and records; six always-running LLM processes are unnecessary.

roles.responsibility: Own the task graph, dispatch, escalation, recovery coordination and retrospective.
Maintain usable handoff context and consistent task packets across sessions.
Independently verify acceptance and issue the quality verdict.
Measure AI behavior and qualify model or harness changes against baselines.
Review trust boundaries, permissions, sensitive operations and injection risks.
Monitor runtime reliability, failure recovery, service health and operational readiness.

recommendedCore.supervisor: One deterministic durable supervisor, not counted as an LLM agent.
recommendedCore.requiredWorkers: Builders remain required on demand, such as fullstack-engineer, frontend-engineer or backend-engineer. Add code-reviewer, product-manager, cto-architect, release-manager and other specialists when scope requires them. The six control roles alone do not build a product.
recommendedCore.limitation: This is a recommended starting structure, not a universal minimum. More role names cannot guarantee autonomy or quality. Human decisions remain necessary at protected boundaries.

modelAndHarnessQuality.promise: Measured quality floors, detected regressions, rejected bad switches and recoverable execution are achievable. Always-best quality with every LLM or harness is not guaranteed.
recommendedSteps: Keep versioned prompts, policies, task state and knowledge outside any model's chat memory.
Define an adapter contract covering tools, refusals, evidence, usage, cancellation and recovery.
Qualify each model, harness, version and task class together.
Compare repeated runs on held-out tasks, adversarial cases and real acceptance checks.
Admit only combinations that meet the required baseline; keep a known-good fallback and rollback.
Hold or escalate when a candidate cannot meet the baseline. Do not weaken checks to pass a switch.
Promote lessons only after evidence and evaluation; retain their provenance and rollback.
